english.title: Permit use of a motor vehicle - tv / film visible to the driver

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: ROAD VEHICLES CONSTRUCTION AND USE REGULATION 1986

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), permitted **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) to drive on a road, namely **(..SPECIFY ROAD AND LOCATION..), a vehicle, namely **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE MAKE AND INDEX NUMBER..), when

(A)_[he]_
(B)_[she]_

was in such a position as to be able to see, directly or by reflection, a

(C)_[television receiving]_
(D)_[cinematographic ]_

apparatus used to display something other than information about the state of the vehicle or its equipment, or about the location of the vehicle and the road on which it was located, or to assist the driver to see the road adjacent to the vehicle or to assist the driver to reach his destination
english.legislation: Contrary to regulation 109 of the Road Vehicles (Construction and Use) Regulations 1986, section 42 of the Road Traffic Act 1988 and Schedule 2 to the Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988.

english.standardstatementoffacts:
At **(..SPECIFY TIME..) on **(..SPECIFY DATE..) the defendant permitted **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) to drive **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE MAKE AND INDEX NUMBER..) on **(..SPECIFY ROAD AND LOCATION..) when

(A)_[he]_
(B)_[she]_

other.penalty:
A fine not exceeding level four on the standard scale if in respect of goods vehicle or vehicle adapted to carry more than eight passengers.

A fine not exceeding level three on the standard scale in any other case.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months
